Reviewer: m3 pool job review-4332, Claude Fable 5.2 (claude-fable-5-2), mkinney / seat `.claude-mkinney`; did not write or refresh this PR.

**Verdict: ready for a maintainer to merge.** This is the first review of this PR. I read the whole diff (3 files). I found no blocker.

Tier: this is not a safety-tier review. The diff changes two test files and adds one decision file. It changes no post, no posted G-code, no check, no simulation and no geometry. No recorded program (`*.nc`, `*.cl`, `examples/catalog/**`) changed: `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl" "examples/**"` is empty.

## What is good
- The derived rows are the same rows. `mill_posts()` gives the same 16 mill posts in the same order as the old `POSTS` table. The four family lists give the same lathe, plasma, wire and sinker posts.
- `NOT_NC` has the same seven exceptions that the old `EXTENSIONS` table had. Each other post declared `nc` in the old table.
- The partition check fails for a duplicate name, a missing `.cps` file, a family name that is not in `BUILTINS`, and an entry in two families or in none.
- A new mill post without goldens still fails: `every_builtin_posts_every_golden_byte_exact` reads `golden/nc/<stem>/`.
- The decision file says what was dropped and why.

## Results, merged with main
Built and tested locally on host m3, in `.claude/worktrees/review-4332`. The trial merge of head 4c5b49c45 with upstream/main c16df4e7d is clean. No GitHub runner was used.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test conformance` | 7 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test comment_escape` | 4 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | 2 steps, 0 failed (`post comment_escape (1 fn)`, `app suites: conformance`) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main` | 6 steps, 0 failed (release) |
| `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` | the diff reaches no heavy lane; none ran |

Extra suites run: none are owed. The diff changes no file under `testdata/`, no fixture, no golden and no import code. I did not run `example_catalog`: the diff touches no post, operation, motion code or catalog file.

## Mutations (run by the reviewer, each one removed after the run)
1. The `richauto` row removed from `NOT_NC`: `every_builtin_declares_its_controls_file_extension` is red (`richauto.cps declares the .nc extension`, left `Some("mmg")`, right `Some("nc")`).
2. One post (`mazak`) skipped without a result in `comment_escape.rs`: `header_notes_use_each_shipped_dialect_and_keep_the_full_surface_bound` is red (`every shipped text post writes both notes`, left 25, right 26).
3. `Haas` filtered out of `mill_posts()`: `every_builtin_registry_entry_compiles` is red (`each registry entry is in exactly one family`).

Mutations 2 and 3 are not the same edits as the author's. The work tree was restored to the trial merge after each one (`git status` is clean).

## Law check (upstream/main `AGENTS.md`)
- No process file changed. Thus no `Process change: yes` line is necessary.
- No snapshot PNG, no `CHANGELOG.md`, no `Cargo.toml` and no new test binary.
- The body has a `Changelog:` line and ends with `Refs #3461`. That is correct for partial work.
- The commit subjects are conventional (`test(post):`, `docs(decisions):`).
- No `crates/ui` change. Thus no screenshots are necessary.
- `conformance.rs` has 521 lines. It had 534 lines on main, so it does not grow.

## Requested before merge
None.

## Notes (not blocking)
1. **Names.** The old registry test spelled out each registry name in order. The new test pins only entry 0 (`Fanuc`). I checked the claim of the decision file: each of the other literal names in `BUILTINS` is a string literal in one or more other test files (for example `first_router_part.rs` for `RichAuto DSP A11`, `after_op.rs` for `Mach3`, `wire_post/sodick_aq600l.rs` for `Sodick Wire EDM (LN2W)`). The Agie name is a constant with alias tests. Thus a rename still fails a test. The order of entries 1 to 26 (the picker order) is not pinned now. Persistence is by name, so this is not a project-file risk.
2. **`comment_escape.rs` count.** Each `.cps` file in the loop now gives a text result, a native refusal, or a panic. The new count assertion fails only for a silent skip (mutation 2). The old number 26 also failed when a file was removed from `assets/posts/`. For a registry post, the new `is_file` check in `conformance.rs` covers this. `waterjet-iso.cps` is not in the registry, so only its own suites cover its removal.
3. **Stacking.** `AGENTS.md` "Overlapping issues stack" says that an overlap stacks or waits. This PR does not stack on #2646 (draft `feat`, `needs-rework`) and does not wait. The decision file records the reason. I agree with the reason: #2646 only adds rows to the tables that this PR removes. The maintainer can overrule it.
4. The body names base 470d1a27c. upstream/main is now c16df4e7d. The merge is clean and the results above are on the merged tree.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
